lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The dates leave nine months between the B.S. and the university web role with no study or work listed.
“Raising bookings per search 9%” is missing “by.”
items.because: The quantified result reads as an editing error.

items.says: Code-splitting does not cut the booking flow’s total JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB.
items.because: The calendar and map code still exists in separate chunks; code-splitting changes how much loads initially.

items.says: The JavaScript reduction is a technical proxy without a user-facing consequence.
items.because: The bullet does not show whether loading, responsiveness, or booking completion improved.

items.says: “The audit” does not identify the accessibility tool, standard, or scope behind the 14 issues.
The comma after “deferring the analytics script” incorrectly separates the subject from its verb.
items.because: The optimization actions collectively form the subject of “raised.”

items.says: The 52-to-91 Lighthouse result is buried after a long list of implementation details.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters four methods before the strongest information.

items.says: Lazy-loading the hero image cannot credibly be credited with the LCP reduction.
items.because: The hero image is commonly the LCP element, and lazy-loading delays its request.

items.says: The claimed benefit to designers lacks evidence of adoption or reduced interruptions.
Converting PNG images to WebP does not reduce the JavaScript bundle.
items.because: Separately served images are static assets, not part of a JavaScript bundle.

items.says: “The findings led to a preview mode” obscures whether you designed, built, or only recommended it.
items.because: The passive construction disconnects your interviews from the implementation and result.

items.says: The bullet about reducing broken pages from 30 to 6 is not placed first in the entry.
items.because: It combines user research, product action, and a substantial measured outcome.

items.says: “Writes” uses the wrong tense for an ended role.
items.because: The Apr–Aug 2024 dates require past tense.

items.says: Writing a checklist alone cannot be credited with reducing failed audits.
items.because: Audit failures decline when a checklist is adopted and used to remediate pages, not merely written.

items.says: “Accessibility checklist” does not show which standard or technical requirements guided the work.
“Search time” does not identify what the 4-to-under-1-second improvement measures.
items.because: Response latency, results rendering, and total task time represent different outcomes.

items.says: “About 900 riders a week” does not define the unit or source of the adoption figure.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it measures unique users, sessions, or something else.

items.says: “Showing live bus arrivals” does not explain how the app obtains or updates arrival data.
The change from 3.0s to 1.5s is a 50% reduction, not a 75% improvement.
items.because: The reduction is 1.5 seconds against a 3.0-second baseline.

items.says: “Cold-start time” does not specify the performance milestone measured at 1.5 seconds.
A rise from 30% to 40% is 10 percentage points, not 10%.
items.because: A 10% relative increase from 30% would produce 33%.

items.says: “Weekly returning riders” names a group of people when the figures describe a rate.
items.because: The metric sounds like a count and a percentage at the same time.

items.says: The retention result omits the baseline period and the rule for classifying a rider as returning.
items.because: Return rates depend on cohort and time-window definitions.

items.says: “By adding saved stops” does not explain the technical mechanism used to implement the feature.
The bullet’s React and TypeScript attribution conflicts with the heading’s Vue attribution.
items.because: The inconsistency makes the actual frontend stack uncertain.

items.says: “Worked on” does not identify the feature you owned or what it enabled.
items.because: A hiring manager cannot distinguish substantial ownership from general assistance.

items.says: “Time-zone changes” uses nonstandard hyphenation.
items.because: “Time zone” is an open compound in this context.

items.says: The calendar component and testing bullet is not placed first in the entry.
items.because: It shows concrete work and difficult cases, unlike the vague opening line.

items.says: “Handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes” does not say what the implementation verified or prevented.
“Its tests” does not identify the testing approach or technical mechanism.
The demo and code handover bullet stops at delivery without stating what followed.
“Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: The product’s correct name is “Storybook.”

items.says: Angular is listed in Skills without an experience or project entry showing where you used it.
items.because: A reader cannot connect the framework to checkable work elsewhere in the résumé.
